Use a render image to have more realistic textures and control over lighting. SNAPSHOT A snapshot is an image similar to a screenshot, generated through the Snapshot function in CLO. Use a snapshot for faster results or to show a design as a sketch. Pay attention not to include color-marking in the 3D window such as strengthening or bonding this could confuse collaborators / vendors. Use images of 3D garments in your tech pack, whether it is a realistic render image or 3D garment in a sketch style, to avoid double work with 2D sketches. Decide how to style those images in terms of avatar and pose and which views and details you want to show. A POSSIBLE WORKFLOW 1. Create a 3D garment. 2. Change the avatar pose. 3. Check if the garment looks correct. Maybe iron it. 4. Use High Resolution. 3D Tool Bar > Hi-Res Garment > Simulate. 5. Decide if the avatar should be visible or not. 6. Create or upload Custom Views. 7. Create Snapshot and / or Render images. 8. Add the images to your tech pack. TIP! In a CLO-SET tech pack, the images will be generated automatically. PDF_Summary: Comprehensive Guide: Using Images in Tech Packs Introduction: - A render is a photorealistic image of a 3D model generated through the rendering process. - A snapshot is an image similar to a screenshot, generated through the Snapshot function in CLO. - Use render images for more realistic textures and control over lighting. - Use snapshots for faster results or to show a design as a sketch. Images Prearrangement: How to Set Up Custom Views: 1. Press 2 on the keyboard for Front View or right-click on the background of the 3D Window and select Front. 2. Save the current front view by clicking the icon of the tiny camera in the top right corner. 3. Rotate around the garment to create other views and save them. 4. Right-click on the Custom View to rename it. 5. Save Custom Views and load them in other projects. 6. Double-click onto a view to switch to it. Pose: - Choose a preferred pose from the library. - Create custom poses if needed. Avatar: - The avatar can be visible in color, white, or hidden completely. - Use the 3D Toggle Bar to toggle between different avatar display options. Trick: Ironing: - Use the Strengthen function to temporarily iron garments for a nicer appearance. - Select all pattern pieces, right-click, and select Strengthen. - Select all pattern pieces again, right-click, and select Unstrengthen. Snapshots: 1. Open the Snapshot window from the Main Menu. 2. Choose Single or Multiview 1 tab for creating one or multiple pictures. 3. Set up custom views by double-clicking on them or selecting them from the drop-down menu. 4. Zoom in on the project. 5. Select options such as Transparent Background, Save Separate Images, and Save All Colorways. 6. Save and load the Snapshot Multiview settings. Style Line: - Use the Style Line function to express style lines, silhouettes, internal/external lines, and fold lines of 3D garments. - Change thickness and choose a contrast color for better visibility. Monochrome Surface: - Use Monochrome Surface to imitate a sketch style combined with Style Line. - Pay attention that graphics are not visible in this mode. Desaturation: - Use desaturation of a fabric to achieve a sketch style without losing graphics. - Change desaturation properties if needed. Dark Colors: - Use a contrast color for style lines when working with dark colors. - Change the color of graphics if they are not visible enough. Quality Render (3D Window): - Use Quality Render (3D Window) to add realism to images. - Always use Quality Render for shiny fabrics and fabrics with transparency. Garment Fit Maps: - Export the Garment Fit Maps information as a Snapshot of the 3D Window or make a screenshot of the 3D Window to include the scale. Render: - Use the Render function to generate photorealistic images of 3D models. - Set up render properties, light properties, and image/video properties. - Use the Interactive Render button to start the real-time render preview. - Click on the Final Render (Image/Video) button to generate the rendered image. Incorporating Images into Tech Packs: - Use the images created (snapshots and render images) in your tech pack. - Combine snapshots and render images to present different types of information. - Include Points of Measure (POM) in your tech pack. - Add comments to 3D images to avoid creating additional 2D sketches. CLO-SET Tech Pack: - If a tech pack has been generated on CLO-SET, the images will be created automatically.

Title: CLO Avatar Editor Guide
PDF_Text: AVATAR EDITOR INTRODUCTION CLO Avatars ASTM Sizing .AVT Vs .AVS Format Avatar Editor AVATAR SIZE Avatar EditorAvatar Size MeasurementsTotal Body MeasurementsDetail WorkflowOpen WorkflowTotal Body WorkflowDetails Saving in .AVS Format Saving in .AVT Format ARRANGEMENT POINTS Arrangement Points Vs Bounding Volumes How to use Arrangement Points Avatar EditorArrangement Points Automated Arrangement Points Creation Transfer Arrangement Points BOUNDING VOLUMES Bounding Volumes Avatar EditorBounding Volume MEASURE Basic Circumference Measurement Vs Surface Circumference Measurement Basic Tape Measurement Vs Surface Tape Measurement Linear measurement Height Measurement Avatar EditorMeasure Attach To Measure (Avatar) TABLE OF CONTENTS INTRODUCTION CLO offers 12 avatars: Avatar Version 1 (V1): 2 male, 2 female Avatar Version 2 (V2): 3 male, 3 female Avatar Kid Version 1 (V1): 1 boy & 1 girl (716 years), 1 kid (26 year), kid (618 month) There is a distinction between V1 Avatars and V2 Avatars. For example, when a size (*.avs) or a pose (*.pose) has been created on a V2 Avatar, it can only be applied on a V2 Avatar. The principle is the same for V1 Avatars. CLO AVATARS Avatar Adult Versions 2 (V2) and Avatar Kid Versions 1 (V1) CLO offers sizes according to the ASTM measurement system such as size grouping Missy Curvy, Missy Straight, Petite Curvy, Petite Straight, Plus Curvy, and Plus Straight for women and sizes 34 to 52 for men. These standard sizes might not suitable for all users. Therefore we offer the possibility of creating and saving a custom size. The ASTM sizing can be found in the Size section of each individual avatar folder. ASTM SIZING US_ ASTM_Missy Curvy T2 US_ ASTM_Missy Curvy T4 US_ ASTM_Missy Curvy T6 US_ ASTM_Missy Curvy T8 US_ ASTM_Missy Curvy T10 US_ ASTM_Missy Curvy T12 US_ ASTM_Missy Curvy T14 US_ ASTM_Missy Curvy T16 US_ ASTM_Missy Curvy T18 US_ ASTM_Missy Curvy T20 .AVT VS .AVS FORMAT AVATAR: AVT FORMAT Contains all the information related to Avatars (Model, Sizing, Poses, Motions, Accessories, Bounding Volumes, Arrangement Points). This type of format allows you to save an OBJ of a human form as an Avatar with its Bounding Volumes and its Arrangement Points. The AVT format also allows you to contain the rig (skeleton) of an Avatar. It is not possible to open an AVT file in other 3D software. This type of format is only compatible with CLO. AVATAR SIZE: AVS FORMAT Contains Avatar Size information. The Avatar file (*.avt) must be loaded before opening the Avatar Size file. AVS files do not contain an Avatar, only size information. It is not possible to mix AVS files between Avatars of different versions and sexes. The AVS file is only compatible with the Avatar on which it was originally created. For example, if you created an AVS file on a female V2 Avatar (regardless of Mara, Grace or Feifei), you will only be able to reopen it on a female V2 Avatar. AVATAR EDITOR AVATAR SIZE Edit a CLO default Avatar or a Size Editable converted Avatar. Specific measurement areas and proportions can be adjusted to further customize avatars. MEASUREMENTS Create Custom Tape Measure markings using Avatar Tape toolsView and rename them in the Measurements list. ARRANGEMENT Edit existing or create custom Arrangement Points & Bounding Volumes to assist in pattern arrangement. The Avatar editor contains three main components: Avatar Size, Measurements and Arrangement. Each section allows for customization of those specific parts. AVATAR SIZE AVATAR EDITORAVATAR SIZE Avatar EditorAvatar Size enables you to edit a CLO default Avatar or a Size Editable converted Avatar Main Menu > Avatar > Avatar Editor > a window appears: first tab Avatar Size Total Height: Controls the height from the heel level to the top of the head. If the Avatar is in heels it will not include the heels and still measure to the heel level. MEASUREMENTSTOTAL BODY HPS Height: Insert the measured height from floor to neck. Use for human body measurements. Inseam: Insert the measured height from the floor to crotch. Use for mannequin measurement. TOTAL BODY Height: Allows you to change the height of the Avatar.Use the drop-down menu on the right to select the height unit. The default unit follows the program unit.There are three different options for controlling a finished body height. Each option adjusts the height from a different control point and can have slightly different outcomes in body proportion. MEASUREMENTSTOTAL BODY Bust Circumference: Change the width of the chest and overall body proportionally by controlling the widest point of the bust area. Under Bust will be available in the details section when Bust Circumference is chosen in Total body Width: Adjust the overall width of the Avatar using the chest circumfmerence as the general control point. All other areas of the body will increasse or decrease proportionally when the width is changed. Female Avatar Options: Bust Circumference or Under Bust Circumference are avilable only for the female Avatars. here is no preference between these two options. However, for some cases where there is a need to change the bust in more detail (for example when trying on a bra) it is advisable to define Under Bust Circumference as the total measure. This will allow you to independently adjust the bust measurement in the Details section of the Avatar Size. Under Bust Circumference: Change the width of the chest and overall body proportionally by controling the Underbust Circumference area. Bust will be available in the details section when underbust is chosed in Total Body * Recomened if the desire is to incresing cup size indepenandly of all other body proportions to mimic cup enlargement or reduciton. * Recomened to use if desire is to increase overall body with to mimin weight gain or loss distribution evenly. MEASUREMENTSTOTAL BODY Width: Change the width of the Avatar by controlling the Chest Circumference All other areas will increase or decrease proportionally in relation to the Chest. Width: Adjust the overall width of the Avatar using the Chest Circumference as the general control point. All other areas of the body will increasse or decrease proportionally when the width is changed. Male Avatar Options: Chest Circumference is the only option available. MEASUREMENT TIP! Configuration of Avatar measurements: Due to technical reasons, a marginal error may be generated even after the insertion of a specific measurement. The margin of error appears in parentheses next to each measurement in the Avatar Editor. The actual measurement (the addition of the inserted measurement + margin of error) can be checked on the avatar in the 3D Window. This margin of error is used to adjust the appearance and proportion of the measurement relative to the rest of the body. We recommend that you take into consideration the measurement displayed in the 3D window and adjust the initial value inserted in the Avatar Editor by adding the margin of error. However there are some technical limitations and the adjustment of the measures may not be optimal. When you are in this type of situation, try to adjust the value to the nearest number. MEASUREMENTSDETAIL BASIC : Allows an option to edit an avatar using basic key measurements. Other areas will adjust proportionally in relation to the basic key measurements. ADVANCEDHUMAN BODY: This is an intermediate version that is best used when trying to replicate the general size of measurements taken from a human. It has more measurement options than the Basic , but less measurements than Advanced Dressform. Many height placement measurements are not accessible here and will be determined by the Total Body Height. ADVANCEDDRESSFORM: This is the most advanced editing option and will have the most measurements accessible for editing. Further height placements will become available to allow a user to adjust height proportions that can be most accurately measured on a dress form. SHOW / HIDE ALL MEASUREMENTS: By default, only editable measures appear in the window. When you select the list icon at the top right of the Details section, you will see greyed-out measures. It is not possible to change the values of these measurements. These values remain greyed out because they automatically adjust in relation to the others so that the body shape looks proportionate and realistic. WORKFLOWOPEN TIP! Start by adding the details of the Basic section, then to go to the Advanced (Human Body) section if your measurements are taken from a real human. If your measurements have been taken from a mannequin, go to Advanced (Dressform) after Basic instead. This will allow the algorithm to better interpret the final result and obtain a more natural form. TIP! On each detail section (basic, advanced, etc.), start with all the Height measurements and then move on to Circumference measurements. STEP 1: Add an Avatar to the workspace. STEP 2: Open the Avatar Editor. WORKFLOWTOTAL BODY STEP 3: Change the Total Body size. If possible, choose HPS Height or Inseam, then Bust Circumference or Under Bust Circumference. STEP 4: In the Details section, start by changing the Basic measures. STEP 5a: Change necessary measurement under Advanced (Human Body) if your measurements were taken from a human body. TIP! Start with all Height measurements before moving on to Circumference measurements. WORKFLOWDETAILS STEP 5b: Go to Advanced (Dressform) section if your measurements were taken from a mannequin. TIP! Start with all Height measurements, before moving on to Circumference measurements. Q&A SHOULD I FOLLOW AN ORDER TO CHANGE THE MEASURES OF EACH SECTION? Yes. It is best to add all the height measurements and then add the circumference measurements. Height measurements have a big influence on how the algorithm interprets the final shape. When you are in the Basic section, first add: CF Neck to Waist, CB Neck to Waist, HPS to Apex, Inseam Height, CB Neck to Wrist, and Total Rise. Then add the circumferences such as: Neck Base, Bust Circumference, Waist Circumference, High Hip Circumference, Low Hip Circumference, Thigh Circumference, and Bicep Circumference. Follow the same procedure for all sections. MY AVATAR DOESNT LOOK NATURAL, WHAT TO DO? Due to certain technical limitations, it sometimes happens that certain parts of the Avatars body appear twisted. In this case it is better to leave aside problematic measures and let the software do an automatic calculation. Generally, the most accurate way to record an Avatar is to do a 3D scan of a body. If you later want to add a rig (skeleton) to this 3D scan, you will have to go through our Convert to Avatar function. Learn more about Convert to Avatar. Warning! Once you have moved from the Basic section to the Advanced (Human Body) and Advanced (Dressform) sections, avoid going back to the previous section because your measurements will reset, by default. SAVING IN .AVS FORMAT TIP! The steps to modify the measurements of an Avatar are the same whether saving an AVT or an AVS file. The only difference is the way you open the file. Avatar Size AVS: Contains Avatar Size information. The Avatar file (*.avt) must be loaded before opening the Avatar Size file. Avatar AVT: Contains all the information related to avatars (Model, Sizing, Poses, Motions, Accessories, Bounding Volumes, Arrangement Points). STEP 1: In the Avatar Editor, click on the Save icon at the top right. STEP 2: A pop-up window will appear and you will be able to save your AVS file. Name your file and save. SAVING IN .AVS FORMAT STEP 3: If you create a size folder and save your AVS file in this folder, you can then connect this folder to your CLO library and click-drag your different sizes on the avatar of your project file. TIP! You can open an AVS file, using the Open Icon, next to Save, in the Avatar Editor. SAVING IN .AVT FORMAT STEP 1: Once you have finished modifying your avatar, you can save it in the AVT format. Menu > File > Save As > Avatar. TIP! If you want to add a custom Avatar in the workspace: File > Open > Avatar ARRANGEMENT POINTS ARRANGEMENT POINTS .ARR Arrangement Points (*.arr) are the blue points that are distributed around the avatar, and are used to arrange patterns around it easily. Arrangement Points are created on top of the Arrangement Bounding Volume covering the surroundings of the Avatar. ARRANGEMENT POINTS VS BOUNDING VOLUMES BOUNDING VOLUMES .PAN Arrangement Bounding Volumes (*.pan) are the green cylinders covering each part of the Avatar, and each end of a cylinder is connected to an Avatars joint. As such, even if the Avatar's Pose is changed, the cylinder simply adjusts to the changed Pose and can be used as it is. To view Arrangement Points, go to the 3D Toggle Bar > Avatar Display > Show Arrangement Points. TIP! Shortcut: SHIFT + F To view Boundary Volumes, go to the 3D Toggle Bar > Avatar Display > Show Boundary Volumes. HOW TO USE ARRANGEMENT POINTS STEP 1:With Arrangement Points appearing around the Avatar, select a pattern and hover the mouse over an Arrangement Point.The Arrangement Point will highlight in a brighter blue.A preview of the pattern placement is being displayed in grey. STEP 2:Select a desired Arrangement Point.The center of the pattern is now being placed according to the selected Arrangement Point. TIP! Symmetric Arrangement occurs as long as the patterns and Arrangement Points have symmetry applied. AVATAR EDITORARRANGEMENT POINTS TIP! Symmetric Arrangement Point Setting Name the Arrangement Point with an underscore and location (R for right and L for left) at the end of the name to set them as Symmetric Arrangement Points. The name must be the same as the name before the underscore and the alphabet. _R _L All arrangement points apart from the Avatar's body are symmetrically set by default. Main Menu > Avatar > Avatar Editor > Arrangement > Point CLO Avatars have their Arrangement Points pre-arranged around the body. If you would like to edit, add or delete any of the Arrangement Points, you can do this through the Avatar EditorArrangement. TIP! The following method applies for any OBJ that you bring into CLO. AVATAR EDITORARRANGEMENT POINTS OPEN Using the Open icon, you can open an ARR file on another OBJ. SAVE Using the Save icon, you can save the create ARR file and open on another Avatar. Note: Some readjustment may be needed on a new Avatar. ADD A new arrangement point called Arrangement Point is now being created at the bottom of the A-Point list in the Arrangement tab. DELETE Select the Arrangement Point from the Arrangement Point list and select the Delete icon. ARRANGEMENT BV Selects the Bounding Volume where the Arrangement Point is to be placed. X Moves the Arrangement Point left and right. Y Moves the Arrangement Point up and down. OFFSET Sets the distance between the Avatar and the Arrangement Point. WRAP DIRECTIONS Options: Up or Down. The direction in which the pattern will be wrapped around the Avatar. AUTOMATED ARRANGEMENT POINTS CREATION TIP! This option works properly only when the imported OBJ is either in T- or A-Pose. Otherwise an error message appears if this function cannot be applied properly. STEP 1:Start by loading an Avatar.Go to Menu > File > Import > OBJ. STEP 2:A pop up window will appear.Ensure Automatically Add Arrangement Points option under Object Type. Note: Load as Avatar is selected by default. Arrangement Points and Bounding Volumes are automatically created and sized based on the loaded OBJ. TRANSFER ARRANGEMENT POINTS Another option instead of Automatically Add Arrangement Points is to Transfer Arrangement Points from a CLO Avatar to your OBJ. STEP 1: Import the custom Avatar.OBJ file format: File > Import > OBJType: Load as AvatarScale: Auto Scale STEP 2: Add CLO Default Avatar.Open the Library > Avatar > right click on desired avatar > Add to WorkspaceLoad Type: AddX, Y, Z Translation: 0 Note: In the 3D Window, you now you have a CLO Avatar and your custom Avatar on top of each other. Mostly likely they do not match, so you need to resize the CLO Avatar. STEP 3: X-Ray JointsAdjust the Pose using X-Ray Joints.Go to the 3D Toogle Bar > Show X-Ray Joints (SHIFT + X).Ensure Show IK Joints is on (Green Points).Select a joint to access the Joint Rotation Gizmo and use the rotation handles to move necessary joints. TIP! If you select the small Avatar hovering next to the Gizmo, it will ensure symmetry. STEP 4: Avatar Size EditorResize the Default CLO Avatar to match custom Avatar.Go to Menu > Avatar > Avatar Editor > Avatar SizeUsing Total Body, adjust the measurements to get as close to your custom Avatars size as possible. TIP! Use the Gizmo to ensure both Avatars are directly on top of each other in the 3D Window. STEP 5: Fit Bounding VolumesGo to 3D Toogle Bar > Show Bounding Volumes. You will notice that the Bounding Volumes no longer match the Avatar. To amend: Menu > Avatar > Avatar Editor > Arrangement, select Fit to Avatar Icon. Now Bounding Volumes will automatically adjust. STEP 6:Delete the Default CLO Avatar by right clicking and selecting Delete Avatar.Save Custom Avatar as AVT to ensure the Arrangement Points and Bounding Volumes remain. TRANSFER ARRANGEMENT POINTS TIP! You cannot use the Avatar Size Editor or X-Ray Joints with your custom Avatar, as these features are only available for CLO Avatars. If you want these features, you need to convert your customer Avatar to a CLO Avatar using Convert to Avatar. Learn more about Convert to Avatar. BOUNDING VOLUMES BOUNDING VOLUMES BOUNDING VOLUMES .PAN Arrangement Bounding Volumes (.pan) are the green cylinders covering each part of the Avatar, and each end of a cylinder is connected to an Avatar's joint. As such, even if the Avatars Pose is changed, the cylinder simply adjusts to the changed Pose and can be used as it is. You can change the size of the Arrangement Bounding Volumes (.pan) in the Avatar Editor. When placing a pattern piece on an Arrangement Point, you will see how it's actually the cylindrical shape of the Bounding Volume that gives the shape of the placed pattern piece. To view Boundary Volumes, go to the 3D Toogle Bar > Avatar Display > Show Boundary Volumes. ADD A new Bounding Volume called Pan is now being created at the bottom of the Bounding Volume list, and its properties appear in the Property Editor. TIP! Add a Bounding Volume to add Arrangement Points. JOINT NAME 0 Sets the beginning location of the Joint (X-ray). JOINT NAME 1 Sets the end location of the Joint (X-ray). HEIGHT Sets the height of the Bounding Volume. RADIUS X (mm) Sets the horizontal radius of the Bounding Volume. RADIUS X (mm) Sets the vertical radius of the Bounding Volume. HANDS Toggle on to extend BV's length to Avatar's hands. When this option is on, the BV will reset. FEET Toggle on to extend BV's length to Avatar's feet. When this option is on, the BV will reset. OPEN Using the Open icon, you can open a PAN file on another Avatar. SAVE Using the Save icon, you can save the created PAN file and Open on another Avatar. Note: Some readjustment may be needed on a new Avatar. DELETE Select the Bounding Volume from the list and select the Delete icon. RESET BOUNDING VOLUMES Using the Reset Bounding Volumes option, you can reset to the original placements after adjustments. FIT TO AVATAR Rearrange Bounding Volume according to current Avatar size when changing its Pose or loading another Avatar's joints. AVATAR EDITORBOUNDING VOLUME MEASURE MEASURE Basic Tape Measure & Surface Tape Measure ToolsThese tools are meant to allow a user to measure areas of an Avatar where default measurement markings are not provided. Additionally pattern outlilne or internal lines can be attached to these tape markingss usisng the Attach to Measure tool. Additonal Tape Measure marking will popullate in the Measure tab of the avatar editor. The markings are simply for documentation and do not become a control point for editing in the Avatar Editor. This set of markings can be saved and re-opened on a same version Avatar, but will not be transferable between Avatar versions or genders. There are 6 Tape Measure tools, 1 Editing tool and 1 Attched to Measure (Avatar) tool (see attached images). To access the Measure window: Main Menu > Avatar > Avatar Editor > Measure BASIC TOOLS: Measure areas close to the body in a straight line or around the widest circumference point. This version is most akin to methods of measuring the body with soft measuing tape. It will graze the surface at the highest or widest points of an Avatar. For Example, when measuing the bust or chest it will graze over the apex peaks, not contourign to the valley area between bust or pectoral areas. SURFACE TOOL: This will hug and follow every counour of an Avatars surface. Unlike the Basic versions, the Surface tape measure will never be susupended in air when following high contourd areas such as a bust. It will follow the contour exactly, almost like drawing on a form with a marker. LINEAR TOOL: This will allow you to measure from any Avatar Surface point to another surface point in a straight line. It can measure through an Avatar to capture depth areas, it is not meant for measuring the surface but instead for measureing depths such as the pelvic depth or neck width straight across HEIGHT: To check the Avatar's height from the ground to a particular point. This will always measure in a 100% straight vertical line. (Especially useful if the Avatar is wearing heels.) BASIC CIRCUMFERENCE MEASUREMENT VS SURFACE CIRCUMFERENCE MEASUREMENT BASIC CIRCUMFERENCE MEASUREMENT Measure a circumference on an Avatar. SURFACE CIRCUMFERENCE MEASUREMENT Measure circumference of the Avatar, such as chest circumference and waist circumference, by going over the curves of the Avatars surface. SURFACE CIRCUMFERENCE MEASUREMENT The same steps as with the Basic Circumference Measurement apply. TIP! To create a straight line, hold SHIFT down after the first point is established. TIP! You can rename your measurement in the Avatar EditorMeasure tab. BASIC TAPE MEASUREMENT VS SURFACE TAPE MEASUREMENT BASIC TAPE MEASUREMENT Measure lengths or circumference areas as you would using a traditional measuring tape, grazing high points to measure lengths in the form of a stright line. To view in list form or give custom names you need the Avatar Editor. LINEAR MEASUREMENT LINEAR MEASUREMENT A Linear Measure runs through the Avatar by connecting the start and end points in a straight line. You can use this tool to measure hip and neck depth. PDF_Summary: tor allows users to edit avatars and customize their sizes, measurements, arrangement points, and bounding volumes. It offers 12 avatars in total, including Avatar Version 1 (V1) with 2 male and 2 female avatars, Avatar Version 2 (V2) with 3 male and 3 female avatars, and Avatar Kid Version 1 (V1) with 1 boy and 1 girl (7-16 years old), 1 kid (2-6 years old), and 1 kid (6-18 months old). There is a distinction between V1 and V2 avatars, and any size or pose created on a V2 avatar can only be applied to a V2 avatar, and the same principle applies to V1 avatars. CLO offers sizes based on the ASTM measurement system, including size groupings for women such as Missy Curvy, Missy Straight, Petite Curvy, Petite Straight, Plus Curvy, and Plus Straight. For men, sizes range from 34 to 52. However, CLO also allows users to create and save custom sizes if the standard sizes are not suitable. The AVT format contains all the information related to avatars, including models, sizing, poses, motions, accessories, bounding volumes, and arrangement points. It allows users to save an OBJ of a human form as an avatar with its bounding volumes and arrangement points. The AVT format is only compatible with CLO and cannot be opened in other 3D software. The AVS format contains avatar size information and is separate from the avatar itself. The AVS file must be loaded after the avatar file, and it is only compatible with the avatar on which it was originally created. AVS files cannot be mixed between avatars of different versions and sexes. The Avatar Editor allows users to edit default avatars or converted avatars that are size editable. Users can adjust specific measurement areas and proportions to further customize avatars. It also allows users to create custom tape measure markings using the avatar tape tools and view and rename them in the measurements list. Users can also edit existing or create custom arrangement points and bounding volumes to assist in pattern arrangement.
